items.title: RT by @Maks_NAFO_FELLA: 🇩🇪German police have detained 2 🇹🇷Turkish citizens in connection with the arson of a Starlink ground station in 🇵🇱Poland. The fire occurred in late September at a Starlink satellite communications station in Wola Krobowska, Masovia, around 40 kilometres south of Warsaw. The facility is run by the Polish state-owned telecom firm Exatel, and links Starlink satellites to ground networks, including providing critical internet security and military communications for 🇺🇦Ukraine. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński described the fire as an act of "hybrid warfare". Polish Special Services Minister Tomasz Siemoniak stated that Polish officials have "no doubt that Russian services" directed the sabotage, using individuals tied to the criminal underworld. The Turkish suspects face charges including sabotage and espionage on behalf of a foreign intelligence service, and they are awaiting extradition to Poland under a European Arrest Warrant. Quick and effective collaboration among the 🇪🇺European law enforcement services - not something we hear in the news every day …

items.title: RT by @Maks_NAFO_FELLA: ‼️🇺🇦 Reuters: NATO Innovation Fund (NIF) President stated that Russia’s invasion of Ukraine is reshaping NATO’s defence technology priorities. The NIF is a €1 billion venture capital fund backed by 24 NATO countries. It is expanding into Poland and opening a presence in Warsaw to identify and accelerate promising dual-use deep-tech innovations, looking beyond traditional defence contractors. He identified technologies to detect, track, and neutralise drones, along with space-based intelligence and reconnaissance, as the most pressing capability needs on NATO’s eastern flank, noting that drone incursions in the region have created a different threat mindset. Lessons from the war have significantly influenced the fund’s investment strategy.

items.summaryUk: Ukrainian President Zelensky has again offered an energy ceasefire with Russia, halting strikes on Russian oil refineries if Russia stops attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

items.title: R to @Osinttechnical: More:
items.summary:
More:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa)
It is clear that Putin does not read Truth Social, and his “shahed” drones follow a different set of instructions. But we in Ukraine immediately supported the idea of an energy ceasefire, as we did more than once for months when we ourselves put forward this idea. We agreed to an energy ceasefire. The American team knows very well what this means for us.
We do not have major oil reserves, large oil export capacity, or dozens of oil refineries. In Ukraine, we have just one oil refinery, and it was badly damaged by Russian strikes long ago. We import large amounts of diesel and other oil products. And I am grateful to all our neighbors, especially Poland, for helping us with our energy needs. For us, the key issue is electricity. Russia started its campaign of strikes against our power generation and power grid years ago. And every winter, including this one, Russians try to make these attacks even more intense – we have power cuts every single day.
For Russia, of course, gasoline shortages and burning oil refineries – because of our strikes in response – are painful. And these are not the same volumes that could be lost because of the crisis in Hormuz. But if Russia wants us to stop our long-range strikes against its oil refineries and oil exports, then Russia must stop its strikes against our energy system and critical infrastructure. This is only fair.
From a speech at the Warsaw Security Forum. (1/3)

But we in Ukraine immediately supported the idea of an energy ceasefire, as we did more than once for months when we ourselves put forward this idea. We agreed to an energy ceasefire. The American team knows very well what this means for us.
We do not have major oil reserves, large oil export capacity, or dozens of oil refineries. In Ukraine, we have just one oil refinery, and it was badly damaged by Russian strikes long ago. We import large amounts of diesel and other oil products. And I am grateful to all our neighbors, especially Poland, for helping us with our energy needs. For us, the key issue is electricity. Russia started its campaign of strikes against our power generation and power grid years ago. And every winter, including this one, Russians try to make these attacks even more intense – we have power cuts every single day.
For Russia, of course, gasoline shortages and burning oil refineries – because of our strikes in response – are painful. And these are not the same volumes that could be lost because of the crisis in Hormuz. But if Russia wants us to stop our long-range strikes against its oil refineries and oil exports, then Russia must stop its strikes against our energy system and critical infrastructure. This is only fair.
From a speech at the Warsaw Security Forum. (1/3)

items.title: R to @Osinttechnical: From Ukrainian President Zelensky:
items.summary:
From Ukrainian President Zelensky:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa)
We had a very detailed discussion with @vonderleyen on virtually all the current areas of our work with the European Union and the decisions needed to support Ukraine. I thanked Ursula for the recent €1.24 billion tranche for defense, which Ukraine has already received. I am grateful for the confirmation that another approximately €3 billion in military support will be allocated as early as next week. These funds will strengthen us.
Of course, I briefed the President on the brutal Russian strikes that continue unabated. Just before our conversation, the Russians struck a power plant in Kyiv with a “shahed” drone, and many districts experienced power outages. Later, there were strikes on energy facilities in the Kharkiv region. And all of this happened AFTER the President of the United States made his statement about an energy ceasefire.
Under these circumstances, reliable support from our partners means real protection for people's lives and a guarantee that the Russians will not be able to break Ukraine. We deeply appreciate all the tangible steps taken to support our defense and our people.
Ursula and I agreed that our teams will have detailed discussions on our next joint actions and the coordination of our steps. We are also preparing to open the negotiating clusters – so that all the remaining clusters are opened by the end of the year. Ukraine’s European path is also a path toward strengthening Europe itself. Thank you!

The diffusion of drone technology and tactics will increase, particularly whenever the Russo-Ukraine war ends. I doubt that we are prepared.
items.summary:
In Latin America, Africa, and the Middle East, we are seeing early drone warfare. I would equate this to where Ukraine and Russia were in 2023. The diffusion of drone technology and tactics will increase, particularly whenever the Russo-Ukraine war ends. I doubt that we are prepared.
Ryan O'Leary (@RyanO_ChosenCoy)
One thing that is becoming more common is “PMC” type and drone companies hiring foreigners who did drones in Ukraine for work. The main problem with that, is that anyone can learn to fly a drone in 14-21 days. Give them 6 weeks and they’ll be hitting targets. What they don’t learn in-depth typically is the tactics behind drones (especially for the 6 monthers) or get a good grasp on signals/frequency and all the overly nerdy shit involved in that realm.
Not understanding frequencies and drone tactics in general will create a lot of scenarios such as this as outside of the Ukrainian war, front areas are not saturated with signals and hundreds of drones flying around so it’s much more easy to pinpoint launch positions and also signal locations.

One thing that is becoming more common is “PMC” type and drone companies hiring foreigners who did drones in Ukraine for work. The main problem with that, is that anyone can learn to fly a drone in 14-21 days. Give them 6 weeks and they’ll be hitting targets. What they don’t learn in-depth typically is the tactics behind drones (especially for the 6 monthers) or get a good grasp on signals/frequency and all the overly nerdy shit involved in that realm.
Not understanding frequencies and drone tactics in general will create a lot of scenarios such as this as outside of the Ukrainian war, front areas are not saturated with signals and hundreds of drones flying around so it’s much more easy to pinpoint launch positions and also signal locations.
